6. Click middle-left again: green → white
7. Click middle-left again: white → gray (I think this happened earlier)
8. etc.
But now, clicking on a white cell changed it to green, not gray. So the cycle might be:
gray → green → white → green → white → ... (once it reaches white, it cycles between green and white)
Or maybe the cycle depends on the cell's position or some other factor.
Actually, wait. Let me re-examine the earlier clicks more carefully. I think I may have misremembered the sequence.

- Top-left: green (changed from gray when I clicked at 50, 25)
- Top-center: green
- Top-right: gray
- Middle-left: green (changed from white when I clicked at 55, 25)
- Middle-center: gray
- Middle-right: white
- Bottom-left: gray
- Bottom-center: white
- Bottom-right: gray
So clicking on a white cell changes it to green. And clicking on a gray cell changes it to green. So the cycle is:
gray → green → white → green → white → ...
Once a cell becomes green, clicking toggles between green and white.
Now, what's the goal? The left grid has purple dots at diamond positions. The right grid should match this pattern. Currently:
- Diamond positions: top-center=green, middle-left=green, middle-right=white, bottom-center=white
- Non-diamond positions: all gray
If the goal is to make all diamond cells the same color (either all green or all white), then I need to click middle-right and bottom-center once each to make them green.
Let me try this.
